activity.title: Sock Pairs
activity.goal: Find two things that are exactly the same, and name their colour.
materials: Clean socks in different colours, in pairs (red, yellow, green and blue are ideal)

steps.caption: Lay them together. Say the colour!

activity.safety: Clean socks in child or adult sizes only: no tiny baby socks, and no tights (they can make a loop). Nothing goes round the neck or over the face. If there is an accident, call your local emergency number.
activity.forAdult: In the story, the sparrow looks for colours for her nest and finds them one by one: red, yellow, green and blue. In this game the child looks for two socks that are exactly the same, and hears the colour’s name with every pair. Finding an exact match is practice in looking closely. Tip the basket onto the floor. Hold up one sock and ask, “Where is its twin?” When the child finds it, lay the two socks side by side and say the colour clearly: “Red!” To make it easier, use only three pairs in very different colours. To make it harder, use socks of similar colours, or ask the child to name the colour. Five to ten minutes is plenty. At the end, put the pairs back in the basket together.
activity.inClass: Each child takes one sock from the basket and walks round to find the child holding its twin. When the two meet, they hold up their socks and say the colour together. One adult for every four children.
